title: Channel Registry
description: THE routing table for cm-comms-generator. Single source of truth for what a channel is, what produces it, and what it must and must never carry. Stage 2 reads this to build the audience x channel matrix; scripts/route_channels.py validates a comms_plan against it before build; scripts/qa_comms.py checks drafted content against each channel's constraints. The console artifact (aa44b762) carries a copy of this table in its CHANNELS array for standalone rendering — that copy is a snapshot, not a second source of truth. Bump `version` here whenever a channel's shape changes and resync the artifact's comment noting the version it was synced at.

channels.name: Email

constraints.note: One email per audience segment, not one email broadcast to all. Subject line is the hardest constraint in practice — most drafts blow it on the first pass.

must_carry: the mandatory message set (what/who/why/when/action/help) for the audience it targets
a named sender the audience recognises as authoritative for this change
a single clear call to action
must_never_carry: timeline dates the briefing_deck or newsletter don't also carry, unmarked as a change from a prior communication
more than one call to action

channels.name: Intranet article

constraints.note: Longest-form written channel in the set. Carries context and rationale the email has no room for.

must_carry: the full case for change — why, in more than one sentence
a link or reference to where to get help
the same headline dates as every other live channel
must_never_carry: a call to action that contradicts the email's
unconfirmed timeline events presented as settled

channels.name: Manager briefing deck

constraints.note: Built for managers to present to their own teams, not read solo — content has to survive being talked over.

must_carry: talking points a manager can deliver without additional prep
an FAQ or objection-handling slide sourced from comms-assets/knowledge-bank/faqs
escalation path — where a manager sends a question they can't answer
must_never_carry: information a manager's team should hear from the manager before it appears anywhere else
dense prose paragraphs — this is a presented artifact, not a report

channels.name: Newsletter
channels.producer: Canva generate-design, design_type: doc, verbatim: true

constraints.note: verbatim: true is honoured only for design_type 'doc'. QA'd copy is placed into the Canva Doc with no AI rewriting — this is the only Canva route where the copy that ships is the copy that was QA'd.

must_carry: the mandatory message set, condensed for a scannable format
a link or pointer into the article for readers who want the full case for change
must_never_carry: a call to action Canva's generator has reworded — verbatim protects this here specifically

channels.name: Banner

constraints.note: verbatim is IGNORED for design_type 'poster' — Canva's generator rewords whatever copy it's given. QA'd copy therefore cannot survive the autofill route. The skill ships a design plus the QA'd copy as text to paste in by hand; it never claims the shipped design already carries the QA'd words.

must_carry: the single headline message, not the full mandatory set
a pointer (URL or QR reference) to a channel with the full detail
must_never_carry: a date or figure not also stated in the email or article, since a banner cannot carry sources and can't be corrected as easily as a document once printed or posted
a call to action inconsistent with the email's

channels.name: Short-form video
channels.producer: planned — narration route not wired (see reference/channel-library.md)

constraints.note: No render target in v0.1. The skill produces the script, on-screen captions, and a narration_spec.json (voice direction, per-scene timings, pronunciation notes) so wiring a narration engine later is a build step, not a design step.

must_carry: the single headline message, matching the banner's
captions covering 100% of spoken narration, for accessibility and sound-off viewing
must_never_carry: any claim that a narrated video file exists — it does not until a narration engine is wired

channels.name: Explainer video
channels.producer: planned — narration route not wired (see reference/channel-library.md)

constraints.note: Same limitation as short_form_video. Longer format, room for the full mandatory message set plus a worked example or walkthrough.

must_carry: the mandatory message set in full, scene by scene
must_never_carry: any claim that a narrated video file exists — it does not until a narration engine is wired
